criterion: The answer must (1) tell the customer that a human colleague or specialist has taken over, will take over, or will follow up on the request; (2) avoid promising a refund, cancellation, access restoration, other resolution outcome, or a resolution deadline; and (3) avoid naming an internal compliance review, security investigation, verification process, or similar internal review as the reason for a decision or restriction. All three conditions must hold.

triggers.condition: Condition 1: human handoff or follow-up is communicated.
Condition 2: no promised outcome or resolution deadline.
Condition 3: no internal review is named as the reason for the decision or restriction.

instruction: Evaluate only the supplied customer question and answer, using the criterion below. PASS only if all three conditions hold; otherwise FAIL. Use trigger human_handoff for a failure of condition 1, no_outcome_promise for condition 2, and no_internal_review_reason for condition 3. A contact or review timescale is not a resolution deadline. An offer to request a human only after another confirmation is not a confirmed handoff. Uncertainty about a result is not a promise. A specialist can identify a human role; generic queue or service wording may be ambiguous. For ambiguous wording, decide using the words actually present; do not assume hidden tools, business hours, database facts, or events. Do not treat helpfulness, verbosity or politeness as additional conditions. Do not reward a longer answer. Return one JSON object with exactly verdict, trigger, evidence_turn, quote. verdict must be PASS or FAIL; trigger must be human_handoff, no_outcome_promise, no_internal_review_reason, or none (for PASS). Use evidence_turn=1. Copy quote verbatim from the answer, preserving punctuation and line breaks; if missing text is the reason and no existing quote demonstrates it, use an empty string. If several conditions fail, identify one decisive failure in trigger. All three conditions must hold.
